name: Asumboa
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.source_named: Checked Glottolog refs and archive.org: only wordlist-level material (Tryon & Hackman 1983); no descriptive phonology/grammar of Asumboa located.

sources.citation: François, Alexandre. 2009. The languages of Vanikoro: three lexicons and one grammar (PL 605:103-126); François 2021, Teanu dictionary introduction (Dictionaria 15).
sources.note: Utupua languages mentioned only for subgrouping; the penultimate-stress statement in François 2021 is for Teanu (Vanikoro), not Asumboa.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.1 languoid page and sources.bib entries for asum1237 (Ray 1926; Tryon & Hackman 1983; Capell 1962; Cashmore 1972 'Vocabularies of the Santa Cruz Islands' ms 78 pp; Grace 1955-56 fieldnotes notebook 45; Ethnologue; UNESCO Atlas).
sources.note: Bibliographic only: no grammar, sketch or phonology entry exists for Asumboa (Glottolog lists no grammar, sketch or phonology); remaining items are wordlists/overviews.
Nothing on phonology; cites only Tryon 1994.

sources.citation: Lynch, John, Malcolm Ross & Terry Crowley. 2002. The Oceanic Languages. Richmond: Curzon. Ch. 5.2 'Utupua and Vanikoro'.
sources.note: Subgrouping remarks only; the only Temotu sketch in the volume is Buma (Vanikoro). Nothing on Asumboa stress.

sources.citation: Tryon, Darrell T. & B. D. Hackman. 1983. Solomon Islands Languages: An Internal Classification (Pacific Linguistics C-72). Canberra: ANU. Asumboa = wordlist no. 100; pp. 70-71 Utupua/Vanikoro sound correspondences.
sources.note: Silent. Phonemic transcriptions without stress marks; the only occurrences of 'stress' are footnotes on vowel reflexes 'in unstressed position' for other languages; no statement of Asumboa stress placement. Notes that Ray produced a grammatical sketch of 'Utupua (Asumboa)' from liturgical materials.

sources.citation: Ray, Sidney H. 1926. A Comparative Study of the Melanesian Island Languages. Cambridge: Cambridge University Press. 'Grammar of the Utupua Language', pp. 461-469 (Glottolog: Utupua (Asumboa) [aua]). Pages 461-465 downloaded as Google Books full-view page scan (id CHAOAAAAYAAJ) and scanned; pp. 466-469 not retrievable (Google blocked further requests).
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: open copy online; also held in print at Harvard (Widener Library (offsite storage), call number 2234.7.25)
sources.note: Silent. Sect. 1 'Alphabet' and 2 'Sounds' (pp.461-462) give vowels a e i o u ö ü, consonants, and letter values ('The g is the Melanesian g; g as ng in finger.. In the MS. the g and n are not always marked'); nothing on accent/stress. Sketch compiled from a MS by Rev. B. Teilo; remaining sections are article, nouns, pronouns, genitive, adjectives, verbs.

sources.citation: Tryon, Darrell. 1994. Language contact and contact-induced language change in the Eastern Outer Islands, Solomon Islands. In Dutton & Tryon (eds), Language Contact and Change in the Austronesian World (Trends in Linguistics 77), 611-648. Berlin: Mouton de Gruyter.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Only modern first-hand account of the three Utupua languages (Tryon's own fieldwork); if any published source gives an Asumboa phonology note including stress, it is this chapter.

sources.citation: Lackey, William & Brenda H. Boerger. 2021. Reexamining the phonological history of Oceanic's Temotu subgroup. Oceanic Linguistics 60(2):367-411.

sources.note: Historical phonology covering Asuboa/Nebao/Tanibili; abstract invokes prosodic conditioning of vowel loss, so it may state (or assume) stress placement for Utupua languages, possibly citing Tryon's field data.
